item.name: Old Lasso
item.cardSummary: Free starter option with enough reach for the first catches, but no power scaling.
item.bestUse: Use only until the first affordable upgrade is available.
item.limitation: No power and short range make stronger animals slow or impractical.

item.name: Wooden Rope
item.cardSummary: Small power step from the starter lasso, traded against the lowest listed range.
item.bestUse: Buy only as a cheap bridge if range is not causing misses.
item.limitation: The short reach makes it awkward once animals move farther away.

item.name: Steel Lasso
item.cardSummary: Early upgrade that keeps the same low power while giving a more comfortable catch radius.
item.bestUse: Use as the first practical range upgrade for basic farming.
item.limitation: Falls behind when rare animals start needing more power.

item.name: Hunter Loop
item.cardSummary: Range-focused early lasso that helps with positioning but does not improve tame power.
item.bestUse: Use when reach matters more than catch strength.
item.limitation: Zero power makes it unreliable for stronger animals.

item.name: Shadow Rope
item.cardSummary: Longer reach than earlier shop options, but its power still stays low for the tier.
item.bestUse: Use as a comfort upgrade while saving for a stronger mid-game option.
item.limitation: The low power makes it a weak long-term Epic choice.

item.name: Dragon Loop
item.cardSummary: Balanced mid-game lasso with a real power jump and slightly better reach.
item.bestUse: Use for routine mid-game catching before late-biome requirements become demanding.
item.limitation: Not strong enough to be the final answer for tougher late-game catches.

item.name: Prism Lasso
item.cardSummary: Large range option for safer targeting, offset by having no listed power.
item.bestUse: Use when reach and learning catch timing matter more than speed.
item.limitation: Zero power can make each tame take longer than stronger lassos.

item.name: Spectral Lasso
item.cardSummary: Strong mid-game power pick with less reach than the widest Rainbow option.
item.bestUse: Use when catch strength matters more than maximum distance.
item.limitation: Its range can feel short in wider late-game spaces.

item.name: Anchor Lasso
item.availability: Gacha; listed with a higher drop rate than other Rainbow lassos
item.cardSummary: High-power Rainbow lasso with the same mid-range reach as other strength-focused picks.
item.bestUse: Use as a strong upgrade when power is the main bottleneck.
item.limitation: The source notes an occasional swap miss issue.

item.name: Sunforge Lasso
item.availability: Shop or Traveling Merchant rotating stock
item.cardSummary: High-end all-rounder with strong power and workable range.
item.bestUse: Use as a reliable late-game bridge when exclusive options are not available.
item.limitation: Merchant stock may rotate, and the source marks it as expensive.

item.name: Trident Lasso
item.availability: Exclusive Shop with Robux or seasonal events
item.cardSummary: Top power with long reach, making it one of the strongest catch-speed options.
item.bestUse: Use for demanding late-game catches when both power and range matter.
item.limitation: Access depends on Robux purchase or event availability.

item.name: Night Veil Lasso
item.cardSummary: Top power with more reach than the other high-power exclusive option.
item.bestUse: Use as a coin-purchased endgame lasso when saving enough cash is realistic.
item.limitation: The listed coin price is extremely high.

item.name: Bone Lasso
item.cardSummary: Longest listed range, with less power than the main endgame strength picks.
item.bestUse: Use when maximum reach is more valuable than fastest catch strength.
item.limitation: Its power is lower than the strongest exclusive lassos.
